{"title":"The three second rule","hook":"Stop posting videos nobody finishes.","script":"[HOOK] Stop posting videos that nobody actually finishes watching all the way through to the end.
Here is the simple three second rule that I personally use for every single edit I make for my clients.
[ZOOM] First, cut absolutely anything that does not earn the next second of attention from your viewer.
That means the long pause before you start talking, every single um and uh, and every restart where you stumbled.
[B-ROLL: timeline with gaps removed] Then make sure you put a brand new picture on the screen every few seconds or so.
A quick punch in counts as a new picture. So does a bold caption, a screen recording, or a cutaway.
[PAUSE] Try doing this on your very next video and then watch what happens to your retention numbers.
[CTA] Follow me for one practical editing rule every single day.","notes":"Borrowed the callout hook and one-tip-per-shot pacing."}
